title: Building a Time Machine for Efficient Recording and Retrieval of High-Volume Network Traffic
authors: Stefan Kornexl, Vern Paxson, Holger Dreger, Anja Feldmann, Robin Sommer
reviewed: Publisher abstract and primary-paper design/evaluation sections
supports: Connection-prefix retention and configurable traffic classes predate this project. Evaluation includes trace-driven efficiency and operational experience.

title: Auditing Inferential Blind Spots A Framework for Evaluating Forensic Coverage in Network Telemetry Architectures
authors: Mehrnoush Vaseghipanah, Sam Jabbehdari, Hamidreza Navidi
type: Primary research preprint; publisher counterpart exists
reviewed: Primary preprint methods, assumptions, supportability and evaluation; indexed journal abstract
supports: Forensic coverage and artifact survivability already have explicit research formulations. This study audits representation-level support, not correctness against incident ground truth.

title: Advancing Network Monitoring with Packet-Level Records and Selective Flow Aggregation
authors: Ina Berenice Fink, Ike Kunze, Pascal Hein, Jan Pennekamp, Benjamin Standaert, Klaus Wehrle, Jan Rüth
type: Primary conference research (IEEE/IFIP NOMS); author lab publication
reviewed: Author-lab abstract and indexed primary-paper method excerpt
supports: HybridMon combines condensed packet records with selective flow aggregation and evaluates monitoring efficiency. Packet/flow trade-offs are established prior art.

title: Introducing Packet-Level Analysis in Programmable Data Planes to Advance Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Roberto Doriguzzi-Corin, Luis Augusto Dias Knob, Luca Mendozzi, Domenico Siracusa, Marco Savi
type: Primary author preprint; associated Computer Networks publication
reviewed: Primary abstract and official authors' repository; publisher full text denied
supports: P4DDLe selectively collects packet features under resource limits for NIDS detection; resource-aware selection is not new.

title: Rethinking Full Packet Capture Evaluating IDS-Triggered PCAP
type: Primary practitioner white paper (SANS), abstract only reviewed
reviewed: Official title, author, publication date and abstract; full PDF not reviewed
supports: A directly related study addresses alert-driven capture versus full capture and forensic usefulness. Its existence narrows any novelty claim; no numerical findings are used.

title: Sampling and Filtering Techniques for IP Packet Selection
reviewed: Official categories and attained selection fraction
supports: Sampling and deterministic property filtering are distinct; configured and attained packet selection fractions may differ.

title: Specification of the IP Flow Information Export IPFIX Protocol for the Exchange of Flow Information
authors: Benoit Claise, Brian Trammell, Paul Aitken
supports: IPFIX exports flow information using template and data records; it does not imply retention of original packet contents.

title: Suricata yaml Conditional PCAP logging
supports: Suricata supports all, alerts and tag conditional PCAP logging. The MVP alert rule is illustrative and does not run Suricata.

title: Common Logs and conn log
reviewed: Official common-log list and connection-log tutorial
supports: Connection, DNS and HTTP logs provide structured monitoring records. Metadata availability is separate from preserved packet evidence.

title: Configure packet capture
reviewed: Indexed official page; direct HTML access denied
supports: Precision capture via triggers and packet slicing are existing commercial mechanisms; no independent effectiveness result is inferred.

title: Introducing Endace
reviewed: Official indexed product material and capture-solution pages
supports: Endace offers continuous capture and discusses triggered capture trade-offs. Vendor claims are not independent benchmarks.

title: Guide to Integrating Forensic Techniques into Incident Response
authors: Karen Kent, Suzanne Chevalier, Tim Grance, Hung Dang
reviewed: Official publication scope and forensic-process material
supports: Network traffic is an incident-response data source; collection, examination, analysis and reporting require provenance and integrity controls.

title: PCAP Capture File Format
type: IETF Internet-Draft draft-ietf-opsawg-pcap-05, work in progress
reviewed: Official file and packet header layouts
supports: Classic PCAP file header and record structure, byte order and timestamp resolution; this is a versioned draft rather than a final RFC.

title: Feature-Sniffer Enabling IoT Forensics in OpenWrt based Wi-Fi Access Points
authors: Fabio Palmese, Alessandro E. C. Redondi, Matteo Cesana
supports: Online feature extraction on OpenWrt avoids retaining large PCAP files; demonstrations concern IoT device/activity classification.

title: Improving the Collection of Digital Evidence
authors: Martin Novak, National Institute of Justice
type: Authoritative agency report on funded FileTSAR research (secondary project account)
reviewed: Official agency article and indexed final-report excerpt; 30 MB final report could not be fetched
supports: FileTSAR includes capture, selective analysis and file reconstruction. Reconstruction tools do not by themselves establish a byte-budget retention optimizer. The agency also records concerns about operational release; this is prior-art context, not a recommendation.

title: IPv4 Address Blocks Reserved for Documentation
authors: Jari Arkko, Michelle Cotton, Leo Vegoda
supports: 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/24 are documentation ranges; the generator writes examples to disk only.

title: editcap
supports: editcap can convert capture containers using -F; converting PCAPNG does not add unsupported protocol analysis.

title: Configure a Rule and Advanced Configurations
reviewed: Indexed official rule and retention configuration documentation
supports: Raw packets and parsed metadata may have separate retention periods. Product availability does not establish forensic utility superiority.
